title: Commission the first funded community and project cycle
summary: From January to March 2027, move the Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities from an initial phase sustained largely through informal coalescing, professional goodwill and enthusiasm towards a more durable funded model for the 2027-28 academic year. Run an open call to identify and support a very small number of funded convenors who can provide consistent leadership across the three communities, normally one or two convenors per community appointed for two academic years. Alongside this, invite proposals for approximately five practice-based projects for each community—around fifteen projects in total—that advance community priorities and development, create useful activity, collaboration, outputs and institutional learning, and are not disconnected projects or a general research-grant scheme. Agree the successful convenors and project portfolio by the end of March, together with written faculty or organisational commitments in principle, the protected-capacity model, reserved funding authority, governance and reporting expectations, and the April-August preparation route required for activity to begin in September 2027. Relevant learning from the Step 4 pilots should inform the process and handover as it becomes available, but completion of the pilots is not a prerequisite for commissioning the funded cycle. The purpose is not to replace the energy, relationships and distributed participation through which the communities have formed, but to provide enough protected leadership and practical project support for that activity to become sustainable, purposeful and institutionally connected.

outputs.title: Open convenor and practice-based project calls delivered
outputs.summary: Coordinated but distinct open calls through which funded convenors and practice-based projects are invited, supported and assessed as parts of one coherent community portfolio.

outputs.title: Funded convenors commissioned for the first three communities
outputs.summary: One or two funded convenors commissioned for each of the three communities, with protected capacity and credible institutional support for a September 2027 start.

outputs.title: First practice-based project portfolio commissioned
outputs.summary: Approximately fifteen practice-based projects commissioned, planned as around five connected to each of the three communities and managed as one coherent portfolio. Cross-community projects have one primary community and count once in the total.

outputs.title: Institutional commitments and commissioning confirmations secured
outputs.summary: The selected portfolio moves beyond a preferred list: the institutional, faculty and funding commitments required for a credible September start are agreed by the end of March.

outputs.title: April-August preparation and community handover route agreed
outputs.summary: A clear route through which successful convenors, project leads, faculties and King's Academy complete the practical preparation required for the funded cycle to begin in September 2027.

existingCapacity.contribution: Own the commissioning process, maintain strategic coherence across the three communities, lead recommendations and ensure selected convenors and projects form a credible portfolio.
Administer communications, applications, panel records, conflicts, commissioning confirmations, conditions, onboarding and readiness tracking using capacity already introduced through Step 2.
Provide first-cycle project control, coordinate dependencies and decisions, and support the handover of commissioning administration into the permanent portfolio model.
Assess convenor and project applications, manage conflicts, consider portfolio coherence and make or recommend transparent commissioning decisions.

existingCapacity.role: Faculty, Finance, HR and organisational implementation input
existingCapacity.contribution: Validate workload and backfill routes, confirm commitments in principle, identify budget and employment processes and complete local arrangements after commissioning.

enablingConditions: Approve and reserve the resource envelope that will become operational through Step 7: 0.1 FTE per community for convening, approximately fifteen 0.1 FTE annual project allocations and up to £1,000 direct expenditure per project, creating indicative annual envelopes of 0.3 FTE convenor capacity, 1.5 FTE project capacity and £15,000 direct project expenditure.
Secure written faculty or organisational commitment in principle for the release, workload allocation or backfill route attached to every selected convenor and project.
Constitute panels with appropriate expertise, representation, delegated authority and conflict-of-interest controls.
Publish clear call documentation, applicant support and a timetable capable of reaching final commissioning decisions by the end of March 2027.

decisions.title: Confirm the convenor and project call model
decisions.summary: Approve the linked but distinct call specifications, eligibility, assessment criteria, selection panels, conflict controls, timetable and applicant-support arrangements before launch.

decisions.title: Confirm the protected-capacity and direct-cost offer
decisions.summary: Approve the offer of 0.1 FTE per community for two-year convenor appointments, approximately fifteen annual 0.1 FTE project allocations—around five per community—and up to £1,000 direct expenditure per project, with actual use beginning through Step 7.

decisions.title: Approve the funded convenors
decisions.summary: Approve one or two convenors for each of the three communities, subject to written faculty or organisational commitment in principle and completion of the identified April-August conditions.

decisions.title: Approve the practice-based project portfolio
decisions.summary: Approve approximately fifteen projects, planned as around five per community, using transparent criteria covering quality, feasibility, strategic relevance, community connection, additionality, potential for adoption or spread, equitable access and overall portfolio balance. Preserve the option not to fill an envelope or to reallocate where proposal quality or readiness does not support the intended volume.

risks.title: Informal mobilisation leads are perceived as pre-selected
risks.mitigation: Use an open process, published criteria, independently constituted panels and explicit conflict management, while recognising pilot experience only as evidence available equally through the assessment process.

risks.title: Faculty or organisational support is nominal rather than implementable
risks.mitigation: Require written commitment in principle and a named local owner before final commissioning, with explicit summer deadlines for completing workload or backfill arrangements.

risks.title: Convenor and project selections do not form a coherent portfolio
risks.mitigation: Select preferred convenors before final project decisions, invite proportionate advice on community fit, and retain independent portfolio-level decision-making through the Innovation Committee.

risks.title: The first calls produce weak or uneven applications
risks.mitigation: Provide accessible briefings and proposal-development support, reach beyond established networks, preserve the option not to allocate all funding, use a reserve list and run a targeted second-stage process where necessary.

risks.title: Commissioning confirmations remain too conditional for applicants to plan
risks.mitigation: Do not describe the cycle as commissioned until funding authority, written local commitment, named implementation owners and deadlines are in place.

risks.title: Funded leadership displaces the goodwill and distributed participation that formed the communities
risks.mitigation: Define convening as enabling and connecting rather than owning the community, use Step 4 continuity material and plan a sensitive handover from informal mobilisation leadership.

risks.title: Project funding becomes a general research-grant scheme or substitutes for ordinary business
risks.mitigation: Require a clear practice-based contribution to one or more communities, additionality to existing responsibilities and tangible educational practice, collaboration or institutional learning.

risks.title: Five projects per community becomes an automatic entitlement or volume target
risks.mitigation: Treat five per community as an indicative planning envelope, retain published quality and additionality thresholds, allow cross-community projects, count each project once through a primary community and leave or reallocate capacity where the evidence does not support an award.

risks.title: Project access reproduces existing inequalities
risks.mitigation: Use broad promotion, proportionate applicant support, accessible processes, representative panels and credible local workload commitments. Ask proposals to explain student partnership where materially relevant and how student contribution will be paid or otherwise formally recognised.

assumptions.title: Community-level convenor capacity
assumptions.summary: The 0.1 FTE allocation applies to each community rather than to each individual convenor and may be divided between one or two appointed convenors.

assumptions.title: Project-level protected capacity
assumptions.summary: The 0.1 FTE allocation applies to each project rather than to each person involved, may be divided across a small team and will be validated through the relevant workload model. Around fifteen projects therefore create an indicative 1.5 FTE annual project-capacity envelope for the first three-community cycle.

assumptions.title: Annual project commissioning and two-year convenor terms
assumptions.summary: Practice-based projects are commissioned for one academic-year cycle, with an indicative planning envelope of around five projects for each community, while convenors are appointed for two academic years subject to satisfactory annual review.

assumptions.title: Delivery investment begins in Step 7
assumptions.summary: Step 5 approves and reserves the future resource commitment. Convenor capacity, project release or backfill and direct project expenditure become operational from September 2027 and are recorded as delivery resource in Step 7 rather than duplicated here.

title: Review the first mobilisation, agree the 2028-29 community portfolio and launch the next calls
summary: From July to August 2027, review the initial mobilisation and pilot operation of the Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities together with the first process for commissioning funded convenors and approximately fifteen practice-based projects. Use this evidence to refine the operating, governance, commissioning and central-support arrangements before the portfolio expands, while recognising that the first funded operating cycle will not begin until September 2027 and therefore cannot yet be evaluated for delivery impact. Establish a proportionate success framework for reach and impact that can be used from the first funded cycle, drawing on the initial pilots to establish baselines where possible and agreeing portfolio expectations, evidence responsibilities and reporting arrangements. Include an equity lens that identifies persistent concentrations or access gaps without creating intrusive reporting. In parallel, look forward to the academic year beginning in September 2028. Review the Education Delivery Framework with the Vice President (Education and Student Success) and the Vice Deans Education to identify and agree the three additional education priorities around which the next Strategic Communities of Practice should be established. Use a concise set of criteria covering strategic relevance, distinctiveness, existing expertise and energy, institutional breadth, community viability and potential to develop practice and influence. Confirm the proposed six-community portfolio for 2028-29, the resource and central-support implications of expansion, and any refinements required to the convenor and practice-based project model. Launch the calls that will be commissioned between January and March 2028, allowing detailed preparation and community formation between April and August ahead of operation from September 2028. The call should seek funded convenors for the three additional communities and approximately five practice-based projects for each of the six communities—around thirty projects in total. Convenors appointed to the original three communities through Step 5 will normally remain in post for the second year of their two-academic-year term.

outputs.title: Initial mobilisation and first commissioning review completed
outputs.summary: A focused review of the first three community pilots and the first convenor and practice-based project commissioning process, identifying what should be retained, refined or resolved before expansion.

outputs.title: Reach and impact success framework established
outputs.summary: A common but proportionate framework through which the portfolio, individual communities and funded projects can demonstrate who they are engaging, the depth and breadth of participation, the practice they develop and spread, and their influence on students and institutional education priorities.

outputs.title: Three additional strategic community themes agreed
outputs.summary: Three additional education priorities agreed as the basis for new Strategic Communities of Practice beginning in September 2028, using concise criteria covering strategic relevance, distinctiveness, existing expertise and energy, institutional breadth, viability and potential for practice development and influence.

outputs.title: Six-community expansion proposition approved
outputs.summary: An approved proposition for the six-community model beginning in September 2028, including refined operating assumptions, annual project commissioning and the central support required to prepare and sustain the larger portfolio.

outputs.title: 2028-29 convenor and practice-based project calls launched
outputs.summary: Calls launched for convenors of the three additional communities and for approximately five practice-based projects for each of the planned six communities—around thirty projects in total—for commissioning through Step 8 between January and March 2028.

existingCapacity.role: Strategic education portfolio sponsorship and theme-setting

Lead the review, develop the reach and impact framework, prepare the expansion proposition and own the revised call design using the capacity introduced through Step 2.
Coordinate evidence, records, consultation, theme review, call documentation and the implementation route for the next commissioning cycle using the capacity introduced through Step 2.
Provide evidence and reflection on the pilot communities, the first commissioning process, workload and backfill arrangements, governance, support and readiness for expansion.
Help define proportionate measures, baselines, data sources, qualitative evidence standards and reporting arrangements that test benefit realisation without creating excessive burden.

newInvestment.rationale: Adds approximately 0.2 FTE to the initial Portfolio Coordinator capacity introduced through Step 2, creating an indicative total of 0.4 FTE to administer six communities, annual calls, commissioning, onboarding, records, reach and impact evidence and continuity as convenors and projects change.

decisions.title: Approve the initial review findings and model refinements
decisions.summary: Agree what the pilot and first commissioning evidence supports changing before expansion, what should be retained and what remains untested until the funded operating cycle has run.

decisions.title: Approve the reach and impact success framework
decisions.summary: Agree the common measure set, definitions, baselines, initial targets or qualitative thresholds, evidence responsibilities and reporting cadence for the first funded and future six-community cycles.

decisions.title: Agree the next three community themes
decisions.summary: Following review of the Education Delivery Framework, the Vice President (Education and Student Success) and Vice Deans Education approve three additional priorities using the agreed criteria for strategic relevance, distinctiveness, institutional breadth, viable founding participation and potential for practice development and influence.

decisions.title: Approve expansion and additional central support
decisions.summary: Confirm the intended six-community portfolio, any refinement to the convenor and project model, and the additional recurrent Portfolio Lead and Portfolio Coordinator capacity required to prepare and sustain expansion.

decisions.title: Authorise the 2028-29 calls

risks.title: The review overclaims evidence from the first mobilisation
risks.mitigation: Separate pilot and commissioning evidence from the performance of the funded cycle, explicitly record what cannot yet be judged and carry those questions into Step 7 evidence collection.

risks.title: Success measures reward visibility rather than meaningful reach or impact
risks.mitigation: Distinguish mailing-list and one-off attendance from active, repeat and contributory participation, combine quantitative evidence with proportionate qualitative judgement and review measures that create perverse incentives.

risks.title: Student-facing or institutional impact is claimed without credible attribution
risks.mitigation: Use contribution language, evidence chains and bounded case studies; do not require direct causal student-outcome claims where the evidence cannot support them.

risks.title: Evidence requirements become too burdensome
risks.mitigation: Use a small common core, reuse normal community and project records, permit theme-specific evidence and make the Portfolio Coordinator responsible for maintaining the portfolio evidence structure.

risks.title: The next themes are strategically attractive but cannot form viable communities
risks.mitigation: Combine senior strategic selection through the Education Delivery Framework with a preliminary viability assessment of expertise, cross-institutional interest, overlap and a route to founding participation.

risks.title: Expansion outpaces central support capacity
risks.mitigation: Make the recurrent support decision before the calls create commitments and adjust the scale, timetable or support model if the additional capacity cannot be secured.

risks.title: The original three convenors are inadvertently destabilised by the next call
risks.mitigation: State clearly that they remain in the second year of their appointments and include those communities only where an exceptional vacancy or documented change requires action.

risks.title: Calls are launched too late or without enough clarity for credible proposals
risks.mitigation: Complete theme, resource, measure and call decisions within the July-August window and publish a clear timetable leading to Step 8 commissioning between January and March 2028.

assumptions.title: Step 6 looks forward to September 2028
assumptions.summary: The principal expansion decision concerns the academic year beginning in September 2028 rather than immediate operation in 2027-28.

assumptions.title: The first funded cycle has not yet run
assumptions.summary: Step 6 can review the initial pilots and commissioning process but cannot evaluate the delivery impact of the funded cycle that begins through Step 7 in September 2027.

assumptions.title: Original convenors remain in post
assumptions.summary: Convenors appointed through Step 5 normally serve through 2027-28 and 2028-29 and therefore do not routinely reapply in the calls launched through this step.

assumptions.title: Projects continue as an annual portfolio
assumptions.summary: Approximately five practice-based projects are commissioned annually for each community, creating an indicative portfolio of around fifteen projects across three communities and around thirty across six. Cross-community projects have one primary community and count once; quality and readiness remain more important than filling every envelope.

assumptions.title: Common core with theme-specific evidence
assumptions.summary: All communities and projects use a small common reach and impact framework, while additional evidence can reflect the distinct contribution and maturity of each theme.

assumptions.title: Baselines precede numerical targets
assumptions.summary: Step 6 uses the initial pilots to establish reliable baselines where possible and then agrees evidence-informed numerical targets or qualitative success thresholds rather than inventing false precision in advance.

title: Operate the first funded three-community cycle
summary: From September 2027 to June 2028, operate the first fully funded Strategic Communities of Practice cycle across Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education. Bring the funded convenors appointed through Step 5 into their roles, activate the agreed release, workload-allocation or backfill arrangements, and deliver a visible programme of community activity aligned to the priorities of each community. Maintain the distributed participation and professional energy through which the communities originally formed, while using protected convenor capacity to provide continuity, connection, purposeful leadership and institutional influence. Deliver approximately fifteen practice-based projects—around five connected to each community—across the portfolio. Each project should use its protected capacity and direct-cost allowance to develop, test or spread useful educational practice, create collaboration and generate institutional learning rather than operating as a disconnected research project. Apply the common reach and impact framework established through Step 6, gathering proportionate evidence of active reach, distributed leadership, practice development and spread, institutional influence and student-facing educational impact. Use termly review points to identify where communities or projects need support, adaptation or escalation, and complete a year-end portfolio account by June 2028 to inform the formal operating-cycle review in Step 9. On the current planning assumptions, the full three-community annual operating model has an indicative cash-equivalent value of approximately £249,000, including continuing central support and community allowances.

outputs.title: Funded community leadership and annual plans operational
outputs.summary: The first funded convenors are active in role, their protected capacity is operating, and each of the three communities has an agreed September-June plan connected to its strategic education purpose.

outputs.title: Three funded community programmes delivered
outputs.summary: A visible and purposeful programme of activity delivered by each community, supporting exchange, collaboration, development of practice and contribution to institutional education priorities.

outputs.title: First funded practice-based project portfolio delivered
outputs.summary: Approximately fifteen funded projects delivered—around five connected to each community—each developing, testing or spreading useful educational practice and contributing to one or more communities.

outputs.title: Reach, impact and institutional influence evidenced
outputs.summary: The common reach and impact framework established in Step 6 is applied proportionately across the live communities and projects, generating usable evidence rather than vanity metrics or unsupported claims.

outputs.title: First funded-cycle portfolio account completed
outputs.summary: A concise but substantive account of the first funded cycle, providing the evidence handoff required for the formal review in Step 9.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide strategic and substantive leadership for the three-community cycle, support and challenge convenors, maintain portfolio coherence, connect community insight to institutional routes and lead termly and annual review using capacity established through Steps 2 and 6.

Coordinate community and project administration, records, budgets, reporting, termly review, reach and impact evidence, governance papers and preparation for the next commissioning cycle using capacity established through Steps 2 and 6.

Provide the continuing £12,000 annual portfolio allowance established in Step 4, equivalent to £4,000 for each of the three communities, for eligible community activity, participation, collaboration, dissemination and outputs.
Review plans and evidence, provide challenge and support, approve material changes, manage escalation and receive the year-end portfolio account.
Maintain the local workload, release or backfill arrangements; support delivery; resolve employment, finance and operational issues; and enable practice to be adopted or spread.

newInvestment.item: Funded convenor protected capacity for the first three communities
newInvestment.estimatedCost: £30,000 annual cash-equivalent, using £10,000 per 0.1 FTE as the current planning assumption
newInvestment.rationale: Activates 0.1 FTE of protected capacity for each of the three communities, shared where co-convenors have been appointed. newInvestment.item: Protected capacity for the first annual practice-based project portfolio
newInvestment.estimatedCost: £150,000 annual cash-equivalent, using £10,000 per 0.1 FTE project envelope
newInvestment.rationale: Activates an indicative 0.1 FTE protected-capacity envelope for each of approximately fifteen projects—around five per community—divisible across a small delivery team. The cash-equivalent is a planning estimate and should be recalculated against the actual grade mix and implementation route.

newInvestment.item: Direct delivery costs for the first practice-based project portfolio
newInvestment.rationale: Provides up to £1,000 for each of approximately fifteen projects for eligible direct costs such as materials, small events, paid or otherwise formally recognised student partnership, accessibility, modest specialist input or dissemination.

enablingConditions: Complete all April-August onboarding, workload, budget, commissioning and readiness actions agreed through Step 5 before the funded cycle begins.
Translate the Step 6 reach and impact framework into practical templates, definitions, evidence responsibilities and termly review arrangements.
Maintain sufficient central capacity to support the live three-community cycle while simultaneously administering the 2028 commissioning and six-community preparation activity.
Keep appropriate faculty, Finance, HR and governance routes available to resolve workload, expenditure, delivery, safeguarding, information-governance or other operational issues promptly.

Community and project plans identify practical access barriers, use accessible participation routes and explain any material student-partnership role, including how student contribution will be paid or otherwise formally recognised.

decisions.title: Approve the three community and project delivery plans
decisions.summary: Confirm that the September-June plans, budgets, reach and impact intentions, responsibilities and risks remain consistent with the commissioned portfolio before substantive delivery begins.

decisions.title: Decide material changes, recovery or reallocation
decisions.summary: Use termly review points to approve significant changes of scope, recovery actions, project closure, use of reserve capacity or reallocation of uncommitted direct expenditure.

decisions.title: Decide exceptional project extensions
decisions.summary: Approve only time-limited and justified extensions beyond June 2028, with clear ownership, residual budget, evidence and an explanation of how the project will remain visible in the annual portfolio account.

decisions.title: Accept the first funded-cycle portfolio account
decisions.summary: Confirm that the year-end account provides a sufficiently complete and balanced evidence handoff for the formal Step 9 review.

risks.title: Approved protected capacity is not usable in practice
risks.mitigation: Track actual release or workload implementation from the start, require named local owners and escalate promptly where commissioned capacity is being absorbed by unchanged duties.

risks.title: Convenors become sole organisers rather than enablers of distributed leadership
risks.mitigation: Use annual plans and termly review to test the breadth of contribution, create explicit routes for members to lead activity and assess depth of participation separately from convenor delivery.

risks.title: Funded projects detach from their communities
risks.mitigation: Require ongoing community connection, include project activity in community programmes and review contribution to shared priorities rather than assessing projects only as standalone outputs.

risks.title: Reach is inflated by nominal membership and one-off attendance
risks.mitigation: Apply the Step 6 definitions consistently and report mailing lists and one-off attendance separately from active, repeat and contributory participation.

risks.title: Evidence collection becomes performative or burdensome
risks.mitigation: Use a small common core, reuse routine records, gather short bounded case studies and remove evidence requests that do not support learning, accountability or a real decision.

risks.title: Student-facing impact is overclaimed
risks.mitigation: Use proportionate contribution evidence, state limitations and avoid asserting direct causation or movement in common outcomes where the timeframe and evidence cannot support it.

risks.title: Performance varies sharply across communities or projects
risks.mitigation: Use termly review to identify variation early, provide tailored support and challenge, agree recovery or re-scope, and preserve transparent evidence rather than smoothing out differences at portfolio level.

risks.title: Expansion activity distracts central support from the live cycle
risks.mitigation: Protect the Step 6 central-capacity increase, plan commissioning activity explicitly and monitor whether support to operating communities or evidence quality is declining as the next portfolio is prepared.

assumptions.title: Convenor capacity is allocated per community
assumptions.summary: Each community has a total 0.1 FTE protected-capacity envelope, shared rather than duplicated where two convenors are appointed.

assumptions.title: Project capacity is allocated per project
assumptions.summary: Each commissioned project has an indicative 0.1 FTE protected-capacity envelope that may be divided across a small team, plus up to £1,000 of eligible direct delivery expenditure. Approximately fifteen projects create a 1.5 FTE and £15,000 direct-cost annual envelope.

assumptions.title: Projects normally complete within the annual cycle
assumptions.summary: The first practice-based project portfolio normally completes by June 2028; extensions are exceptional and do not silently roll into the next annual commissioning cycle.

assumptions.title: Step 6 success definitions are operational before evidence is due
assumptions.summary: The reach and impact baselines, targets or qualitative thresholds, definitions, templates and ownership arrangements established through Step 6 are available early enough to shape delivery and termly review.

assumptions.title: Previously established recurrent capacity is not counted twice
assumptions.summary: The base community activity allowance and central Portfolio Lead and Coordinator capacity established through Steps 2, 4 and 6 remain visible as continuing capacity but are not duplicated as new Step 7 investment.

assumptions.title: Projects are connected to a primary community
assumptions.summary: The planning model provides around five projects for each community. Cross-community projects are encouraged where useful but have one primary community and count once in the approximately fifteen-project total.

title: Commission the expanded six-community portfolio
summary: From January to March 2028, commission the expanded Strategic Communities of Practice portfolio for the academic year beginning in September 2028. Appoint one or two funded convenors for each of the three additional community themes agreed through Step 6, for two academic years covering 2028-29 and 2029-30. The convenors of the original Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities remain in post for the second year of their Step 5 appointments and are not routinely recommissioned. Alongside this, commission approximately five practice-based projects for each of the six communities—around thirty projects in total—for delivery during 2028-29, using evidence from the live Step 7 cycle where it is available without making completion of that cycle a prerequisite. Secure written faculty or organisational commitments, reserve the protected-capacity and project resources required for September, and establish the April-August route through which the three new communities form founding networks, convenors are onboarded, projects are prepared and all six communities reach operational readiness. Approve the additional £12,000 annual recurrent base activity allowance required for the three new communities, bringing the six-community allowance to £24,000 from September 2028. In recognition of the move from three communities and around fifteen projects to six communities and around thirty projects, approve a further indicative 0.2 FTE Portfolio Lead and 0.4 FTE Portfolio Coordinator, bringing central support to 0.4 FTE and 0.8 FTE respectively from September 2028. Step 8 creates and records the commissioning commitments; convenor capacity, project capacity and direct project expenditure become operational through Step 10.

Administer applications, panels, conflicts, commitments, conditions, onboarding, community-formation records and readiness tracking using capacity confirmed through Step 6.
Assess applications, manage conflicts, consider portfolio coherence and make or recommend transparent commissioning decisions.

existingCapacity.role: Faculty, Finance, HR and organisational implementation input

risks.title: Strategically selected themes do not develop viable communities
risks.mitigation: Require a founding-network and viability plan, map relevant expertise and relationships, and use April-August for active community formation rather than assuming appointments alone create a community.

risks.title: Five projects per community becomes an inflexible quota
risks.mitigation: Treat five as an indicative planning envelope, apply common quality and additionality thresholds, allow cross-community projects with one primary community, and preserve the option not to fill or to reallocate capacity where readiness or proposal quality does not support an award.

risks.title: Incomplete Step 7 evidence is overused or ignored
risks.mitigation: Use available operational learning proportionately, record what remains unknown and avoid making completion of the first cycle a gate for the next academic year.

risks.title: Expansion commissioning undermines support for the live cycle
risks.mitigation: Protect the central capacity agreed through Step 6, separate current-cycle and future-cycle records, and monitor workload through the Innovation Committee.

risks.title: The second cohort is perceived as secondary to the original communities
risks.mitigation: Use common role, funding, governance and evidence expectations while allowing proportionate differences in maturity and formation.

assumptions.title: Staggered two-year convenor cycle
assumptions.summary: The original three convenor teams continue through 2028-29, while the three additional teams are appointed for 2028-29 and 2029-30.

assumptions.title: Single annual project portfolio
assumptions.summary: Approximately five projects are commissioned for each of the six communities—around thirty in total—within one quality-led portfolio. Cross-community projects have one primary community and count once; the planning envelope is not an obligation to fund weak proposals.

assumptions.title: Commissioning precedes operation
assumptions.summary: Step 8 approves and reserves convenor and project resources; their actual use begins through Step 10 in September 2028.

assumptions.title: Expanded base activity funding is recurrent
assumptions.summary: The additional £12,000 annual allowance creates a recurrent commitment so that all six communities have an equivalent £4,000 annual activity envelope.

title: Review the first funded cycle, refine the model and launch the 2029-30 calls
summary: From July to August 2028, complete the first formal review of a funded Strategic Communities of Practice operating cycle. Use the Step 7 year-end portfolio account to assess the performance of the Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities and their approximately fifteen practice-based projects against the reach and impact framework established through Step 6. Review active and sustained participation, distributed leadership, practice development and spread, institutional influence, student-facing contribution, project delivery, expenditure, workload arrangements, governance and variation between communities. Alongside this, review the Step 8 expansion commissioning and the readiness of the three additional communities for operation from September 2028. Agree proportionate refinements to the operating, support, evidence and commissioning model without judging early-stage communities against expectations that only mature communities could meet. Confirm that the six-community portfolio and expanded central support arrangements remain credible, then launch the 2029-30 annual practice-based project call with an indicative envelope of around five projects for each community—around thirty projects in total—and the next convenor call for the original three communities, whose first two-year appointments end in August 2029. Convenors appointed for the three additional communities through Step 8 remain in post for their second year and are not routinely asked to reapply.

outputs.title: First funded operating-cycle review completed
outputs.summary: A formal evidence-informed review of the first funded three-community cycle and its practice-based project portfolio.

outputs.title: Expansion readiness and six-community operating model confirmed
outputs.summary: A confirmed and, where necessary, refined operating proposition for the six-community portfolio beginning in September 2028.

outputs.title: Reach and impact framework refined for the six-community cycle
outputs.summary: The common measures, baselines, thresholds, evidence standards and reporting arrangements refined using the first complete funded-year evidence.

outputs.title: 2029-31 convenor call launched for the original three communities
outputs.summary: An open call launched for the next two-year convenor term of the Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities, for commissioning through Step 11.

outputs.title: 2029-30 annual practice-based project call launched
outputs.summary: The next annual call launched for approximately five projects for each of the six communities—around thirty projects in total—for commissioning through Step 11 and delivery from September 2029.

existingCapacity.contribution: Lead the first funded-cycle review, formulate operating-model refinements, assess expansion readiness and own the next convenor and project calls.
Assemble evidence, maintain the decision and issue record, coordinate readiness checks, update call documentation and launch the 2029-30 processes.

decisions.title: Confirm the six-community operating start
decisions.summary: Confirm readiness for September 2028 or approve a documented adjustment for any community whose conditions are not sufficiently complete.

decisions.title: Approve operating and evidence refinements

decisions.title: Approve recovery, continuation or closure actions
decisions.summary: Determine the response to material community or project underperformance, non-delivery, unresolved risk or evidence of limited viability.

decisions.title: Approve the 2029-30 call package
decisions.summary: Authorise the convenor call for the original three communities and the annual project call with an indicative envelope of around five projects per community—around thirty across all six communities.

risks.title: The first funded year is judged against mature-system expectations
risks.mitigation: Use the agreed baselines and maturity-aware evidence standards, distinguish trajectory from established impact and record where longer follow-up is needed.

risks.title: Expansion pressures bias the review towards a positive conclusion
risks.mitigation: Separate evidence, judgement and readiness decisions; record material weaknesses transparently; and preserve the option to delay or condition activation for a specific community.

risks.title: Reach is inflated by mailing lists and one-off attendance
risks.mitigation: Use the active, repeat and contributory definitions established through Step 6 and report nominal reach separately.

risks.title: Serving convenors are treated as automatically renewable
risks.mitigation: Launch an open and transparent call for the original three communities, allow incumbents to apply and distinguish performance review from applicant selection.

risks.title: Review and call launch overload central and community capacity
risks.mitigation: Use standard evidence templates, prepare the year-end account through Step 7, protect the central capacity agreed through Step 6 and avoid reopening settled design questions without evidence.

risks.title: New communities are compared unfairly with established communities
risks.mitigation: Use common core measures but interpret evidence against stage of development, founding-network strength and the intended first-year trajectory.

assumptions.title: The six-community portfolio remains the intended scale
assumptions.summary: The review tests readiness and may adjust a specific community or element, but the agreed strategic direction remains a six-community model from September 2028.

assumptions.title: Convenor cohorts remain staggered
assumptions.summary: The original three appointments end in August 2029 and are recruited through this call; the additional three appointments continue through August 2030.

assumptions.title: Project commissioning remains annual
assumptions.summary: A fresh portfolio of approximately five projects per community—around thirty projects across six communities—is commissioned for each academic year, with quality thresholds and cross-community flexibility retained.

assumptions.title: No automatic new investment is created by review
assumptions.summary: Step 9 may identify a case for changed resource, but no additional cost is assumed unless it is explicitly approved and recorded through a later decision.

title: Operate the six-community portfolio
summary: From September 2028 to June 2029, operate the expanded six-community Strategic Communities of Practice portfolio. The convenors of the original Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities enter the second year of their Step 5 appointments, while the convenors of the three additional communities begin the first year of their Step 8 appointments. Activate the full 0.6 FTE convenor capacity and £24,000 annual community activity allowance, and support all six communities to deliver visible programmes aligned to their strategic education priorities while enabling participation and leadership beyond the funded convenors. Deliver approximately thirty practice-based projects—around five connected to each community—supported by approximately 3.0 FTE of protected project capacity and up to £30,000 of direct project expenditure. Operate with the expanded indicative central support baseline of 0.4 FTE Portfolio Lead and 0.8 FTE Portfolio Coordinator. Apply the refined reach and impact framework from Step 9, recognising differences in maturity while maintaining common expectations for active reach, distributed leadership, practice development and spread, institutional influence and student-facing contribution. Use termly portfolio reviews to support, challenge, recover or re-scope activity and complete a year-end six-community portfolio account by June 2029 to inform the permanent-model review in Step 12. On current planning assumptions, the complete annual six-community model has an indicative cash-equivalent value of approximately £498,000.

outputs.title: Staggered six-community leadership model operational
outputs.summary: All six communities have funded leadership, protected capacity and annual plans operating through a deliberately staggered two-cohort convenor model.

outputs.title: Six community programmes delivered

outputs.summary: The refined reach and impact framework applied across all six communities and the annual project portfolio, producing comparable core evidence and useful theme-specific learning.

outputs.summary: A year-end account of the first six-community operating cycle, providing the principal evidence handoff for the permanent-model review in Step 12.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide strategic leadership, support and challenge across six communities and around thirty projects, maintain coherence between the two convenor cohorts, connect insight to institutional routes and lead portfolio review using capacity established through Steps 2, 6 and 8.

Coordinate six-community and approximately thirty-project administration, records, budgets, termly review, reach and impact evidence, governance papers, onboarding and succession processes using capacity established through Steps 2, 6 and 8.

Provide the continuing £24,000 annual portfolio allowance, equivalent to £4,000 for each of six communities, funded through the original Step 4 commitment and the additional recurrent commitment approved in Step 8.
Review plans and evidence, provide challenge and support, approve material changes, manage escalation and receive the year-end portfolio account.
Maintain local protected-capacity arrangements, support delivery, resolve operational barriers and enable developed practice to be adopted or spread.

newInvestment.rationale: Activates 0.1 FTE of protected capacity for each of six communities, shared where co-convenors are appointed. The estimate should be recalculated against named grades and local release, allocation or backfill routes.

newInvestment.rationale: Provides up to £1,000 for each of approximately thirty projects for eligible direct costs including materials, small events, paid or otherwise formally recognised student partnership, accessibility, modest specialist input or dissemination.

Implement the operating and reach and impact refinements approved through Step 9 in all six community and project plans.
Maintain the £24,000 annual community activity budget and the protected central support capacity confirmed for six-community operation.

decisions.title: Approve annual community and project plans
decisions.summary: Confirm that all six community plans and the funded project plans meet the agreed purpose, resource, evidence, governance and readiness requirements.

decisions.title: Determine termly recovery or escalation action
decisions.summary: Approve support, re-scope, reallocation, recovery or closure where activity, participation, project delivery, expenditure or evidence materially departs from the agreed plan.

decisions.title: Accept the six-community portfolio account
decisions.summary: Determine whether the year-end evidence is complete and credible enough to support the permanent-model review in Step 12.

risks.title: The two convenor cohorts create fragmentation or unequal status
risks.mitigation: Use common role and resource expectations, shared portfolio forums and clear cohort-aware succession planning while recognising different community maturity.

risks.title: The five-project-per-community envelope drives volume rather than value
risks.mitigation: Use quality, additionality and community-connection thresholds, permit fewer awards where needed, allow cross-community projects with one primary community and review whether the volume remains administratively and educationally worthwhile.

risks.title: The original communities lose momentum during convenor succession
risks.mitigation: Begin succession through Steps 9 and 11, maintain serving convenor accountability through June and plan a documented handover before September 2029.

risks.title: New communities struggle to move from formation into active practice
risks.mitigation: Use termly readiness and delivery reviews, targeted support from the Portfolio Lead and cross-community mentoring without lowering the requirement for purposeful activity.

risks.title: Central support is insufficient for six live communities and annual commissioning
risks.mitigation: Track actual leadership and administrative demand, prioritise standard processes and route any evidenced structural shortfall into the Step 12 permanent-model decision.

risks.title: Evidence collection becomes performative at larger scale
risks.mitigation: Retain the common core, remove low-value reporting, use existing records where possible and focus evidence on decisions, learning and benefit realisation.

risks.title: Strategic themes drift into disconnected activity programmes
risks.mitigation: Require annual plans and outputs to retain a clear relationship to the Education Delivery Framework and route community insight into relevant institutional decisions.

assumptions.title: Six communities operate with equal base funding
assumptions.summary: Each community has a 0.1 FTE convenor envelope and £4,000 annual activity allowance, while programme and impact expectations remain proportionate to theme and maturity.

assumptions.title: The two convenor cohorts overlap intentionally
assumptions.summary: The original cohort serves its second year while the additional cohort serves its first, creating continuity and a staggered future renewal cycle.

assumptions.title: Annual projects remain portfolio-wide
assumptions.summary: Approximately five projects operate for each community—around thirty across the portfolio—and are selected through common quality and coherence standards. Cross-community projects have one primary community and count once.

assumptions.title: Permanent settlement follows evidence
assumptions.summary: Step 10 operates the intended six-community model, but the final recurrent model and any adjusted support requirement are confirmed through Step 12 rather than assumed here.

title: Commission the 2029-30 portfolio and prepare institutional handover
summary: From January to March 2029, commission the Strategic Communities of Practice portfolio for the academic year beginning in September 2029 and prepare the operating model for institutional handover. Appoint one or two funded convenors for the next two-year term of the original Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities, covering 2029-30 and 2030-31. The convenors of the three additional communities appointed through Step 8 remain in post for the second year of their 2028-30 terms and are not routinely recommissioned. Commission approximately five practice-based projects for each community—around thirty projects across the full six-community portfolio—for 2029-30, using available evidence from the live Step 10 cycle without making completion of that cycle a prerequisite. Secure written faculty or organisational commitments and reserve the protected-capacity and direct-cost resources needed from September 2029. Complete the April-August succession, onboarding and readiness route, and assemble the governance, budget, process, records, minimum viable toolkit and ownership material required for the permanent model to transfer into King’s Academy after the Step 12 decision. This step commissions and prepares the first portfolio that will operate under business-as-usual arrangements; the permanent settlement itself is confirmed through Step 12 and activated through Step 13.

Assess incumbent and new applicants, commission the project portfolio, manage conflicts and make transparent quality and balance judgements.

risks.mitigation: Use an open call, transparent published criteria and separate performance evidence from applicant assessment and formal selection.

assumptions.title: The annual project portfolio remains approximately five projects per community

assumptions.summary: The six-community activity allowance, central support and operating envelopes remain available subject to Step 12 confirmation of the permanent settlement.

title: Review the six-community cycle and confirm the permanent model
summary: From July to August 2029, complete the formal review of the first full six-community operating cycle and confirm the permanent Strategic Communities of Practice model. Use the Step 10 portfolio account and the Step 11 commissioning and handover-readiness evidence to assess reach, participation, distributed leadership, practice development and spread, institutional influence, student-facing contribution, project delivery, expenditure, workload implementation, governance, support demand and differences in community maturity. Confirm or refine the six-community scale, staggered two-year convenor model, annual planning envelope of approximately five projects per community, common reach and impact framework, annual operating rhythm and the role of King’s Academy and the Innovation Committee. Confirm a clear lifecycle route through which communities can be renewed, supported, redefined, paused, closed or replaced where evidence or strategic priorities require it. Approve the permanent recurrent resource settlement, including the indicative 0.4 FTE Portfolio Lead, 0.8 FTE Portfolio Coordinator, 0.6 FTE convenor envelope, approximately 3.0 FTE annual project envelope, £24,000 annual community activity allowance and £30,000 annual direct project-cost allowance. On the current planning assumptions this is an annual cash-equivalent envelope of approximately £498,000, subject to grade-based valuation and confirmation of budget ownership and implementation routes before handover. Launch the 2030-31 annual project call across all six communities and the next convenor call for the three additional communities, whose first terms end in August 2030. Approve the institutional handover pack and the conditions through which Step 13 will activate business-as-usual ownership from September 2029.

outputs.title: Permanent SCoP operating and governance model approved

outputs.title: Permanent recurrent resource settlement approved

Grade-based values, budget ownership and funding routes are confirmed without double-counting earlier BAU liabilities.

outputs.summary: The evidence and review arrangements refined into a sustainable BAU framework that supports learning, accountability and portfolio decisions.

outputs.title: 2030-31 calls and BAU handover authorised

Provide the tested administrative, financial, evidence, governance and annual-cycle coordination baseline for six communities and approximately thirty annual projects.
Continue the £24,000 annual portfolio allowance, equivalent to £4,000 for each retained community, using the recurrent commitments already recorded through Steps 4 and 8.
Review the evidence, approve the permanent model and settle ownership, budgets, delegated authority and recurrent funding.

risks.title: The permanent decision simply ratifies the intended model
risks.mitigation: Use the six-community evidence to test scale, support, funding, governance and value and record any variance from the established assumptions explicitly.

risks.title: Permanent FTE is approved without a workable cash or workload route
risks.mitigation: Use the current £10,000 per 0.1 FTE academic-capacity assumption only for planning, then require grade-based valuation, named funding sources and implementable release, allocation or backfill mechanisms before handover.

risks.mitigation: Confirm previously recorded central-support and community-activity liabilities rather than re-entering them, and record only genuinely new permanent commitments or changes.

risks.title: Communities become permanent regardless of evidence or strategic relevance
risks.mitigation: Retain annual review and a formal route to support, redefine, replace or close a community through evidence and Education Delivery Framework priorities.

risks.title: The evidence framework becomes burdensome in BAU
risks.mitigation: Retain the small common core, remove low-value reporting and focus data collection on decisions, learning and benefit realisation.

risks.title: The handover is approved while key operational actions remain unresolved
risks.mitigation: Use the Step 11 handover pack, assign every open action and make Step 13 activation conditional on budgets, authority, systems and records being ready.

title: Transition to business as usual
summary: From September to December 2029, execute the transition of the Strategic Communities of Practice portfolio into business as usual using the permanent model and resource settlement approved through Step 12. Activate King’s Academy as the accountable institutional owner, put the permanent Portfolio Lead and Portfolio Coordinator arrangements into effect, transfer budgets, records, systems, governance and decision rights, and retire temporary mobilisation dependencies. Begin the 2029-30 operating cycle under the permanent arrangements for the retained community portfolio and commissioned annual projects. Where Step 12 confirms the planned six-community model, the original three communities enter the first year of their Step 11 convenor terms and the additional three communities enter the second year of their Step 8 terms, with approximately thirty projects operating across the portfolio. Embed the recurring annual calendar, including the 2030-31 calls launched through Step 12 and the first BAU commissioning window from January to March 2030. Complete knowledge transfer from Mark Peace and other mobilisation contributors, including the minimum viable operating toolkit, close residual mobilisation actions or assign them into ordinary governance, complete an initial 90-day BAU assurance check, and schedule the later strategic review. Step 13 does not redesign or re-cost the model; it makes the approved settlement operational and closes the mobilisation programme.

decisions.title: Activate the first BAU cycle
decisions.summary: Confirm that the retained communities, commissioned projects and recurring annual processes can operate from September 2029 under the permanent model.

decisions.title: Close mobilisation
decisions.summary: Confirm that temporary mobilisation arrangements can end and that all residual actions and risks have been accepted by named BAU owners.

risks.title: The handover changes labels but not real ownership
risks.mitigation: Require named protected roles, delegated authority, budgets, systems access and acceptance of live records before closure.

risks.title: Temporary mobilisation support is removed too early
risks.mitigation: Use staged handover, retain short defined overlap where necessary and close temporary arrangements only after operational readiness is evidenced.

risks.title: The first BAU year is disrupted by simultaneous transition and operation
risks.mitigation: Commission and prepare the 2029-30 portfolio through Step 11, approve the settlement through Step 12 and use standard readiness checks before September.

risks.title: Annual processes drift after programme closure
risks.mitigation: Enter the full rhythm into institutional calendars, assign recurring owners and schedule the first BAU assurance review before closure.

risks.title: Knowledge or access remains personal to individuals
risks.mitigation: Complete the records and systems inventory, transfer ownership and test access before accepting the handover.

risks.title: Future strategic relevance is not revisited
risks.mitigation: Retain annual evidence review and schedule a later strategic review of themes, scale and alignment with the Education Delivery Framework.

assumptions.title: Step 12 approval is complete
assumptions.summary: Step 13 executes an approved model and does not reopen the permanent policy or resource settlement.

assumptions.title: King's Academy is the permanent institutional owner
assumptions.summary: The portfolio is embedded within King's Academy with governance through the Innovation Committee or approved successor governance body and the agreed senior education routes.

assumptions.title: The 2029-30 portfolio is the first BAU operating cycle
assumptions.summary: The retained communities and projects commissioned through Step 11 begin under permanent arrangements from September 2029.

assumptions.title: No new investment is created by transition
assumptions.summary: Step 13 activates the recurrent commitments approved and recorded through earlier steps rather than adding another layer of cost.
